answer: Practically, the chain should stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because echo only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. In practice opal is enforced by the ledger itself: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
